chapterName: Empire: The Year of Four Emperors and the Flavians (AD 69-96)

questions.question: Josephus, a Jewish commander turned historian, claimed that Titus tried to save the Second Temple. What do most modern scholars think of this claim?
options: They think the Temple survived and was razed years later
They accept it, since he watched from the Roman side
They think Vespasian ordered the burning from Rome
They accept it but believe the soldiers disobeyed orders
They think rebel factions burned the Temple to deny it to Rome
questions.explanation: Most modern scholars doubt Josephus's claim; some suspect he was protecting Titus's reputation.
questions.sourceQuote: Most modern scholars doubt this. Some suspect he was protecting Titus's reputation; several see the destruction as deliberate.

questions.question: Which troops moved first on Vespasian's behalf, invading Italy in 69?
options: The legions of the lower Rhine
questions.explanation: The Danube legions invaded Italy for Vespasian and crushed Vitellius's army at the Second Battle of Bedriacum on 24 October 69.
questions.sourceQuote: The legions of the Danube moved first on his behalf, invading Italy and crushing Vitellius's army at the Second Battle of Bedriacum on 24 October.

questions.question: Which buildings did the three-day fire that swept Rome in AD 80 destroy? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The fire destroyed the rebuilt temple of Jupiter and the Pantheon. According to one ancient biographer, a plague struck at the same time.
questions.sourceQuote: In 80 a three-day fire swept Rome, destroying the rebuilt temple of Jupiter and the Pantheon, and according to one ancient biographer a plague struck at the same time.

questions.question: What made Vespasian a formidable contender for the throne in 69? (select all that apply)
options: Command of four legions, nearly 80,000 men
The loyalty of the Rhine legions
A promise of 30,000 sesterces to each Praetorian
Having Egypt, the source of Rome's grain, within reach
Backing from the Senate from the start
questions.explanation: Vespasian had four legions, nearly 80,000 men, and Egypt, Rome's grain source, within reach. He could not claim descent from the first emperors, and the Rhine legions backed Vitellius.
questions.sourceQuote: With four legions, nearly 80,000 men, and Egypt, the source of Rome's grain, within reach, he was a formidable contender.

questions.question: Which statements about the fall of Vitellius are true? (select all that apply)
options: Beyond his veterans from Germany he had little support
He was killed in the Forum and his head put on a pole
He fled to Gaul and died in exile there
He was caught in the palace and killed on 20 December 69
He took his own life after losing at Bedriacum
His position collapsed when the eastern armies declared for Vespasian
questions.explanation: With little support beyond his German veterans, Vitellius collapsed once the eastern armies backed Vespasian, and he was killed in the palace on 20 December 69. Suicide after Bedriacum was the fate of his predecessor.
questions.sourceQuote: When the eastern armies declared for Vespasian, his position collapsed.

questions.question: What was unusual about the governor in Gaul who launched the revolt of 68?
options: He belonged to the ruling family and sought the throne
He commanded the Rhine legions that later backed Vitellius
He was a centurion's grandson who later founded a dynasty
He was of humble origins and did not want the throne himself
He was an elderly, childless senator from Spain
He was a former Praetorian commander bribed by Galba
questions.explanation: The rebel governor was a man of humble origins who did not want the throne and went looking for a candidate instead. He found one in Galba.
questions.sourceQuote: In March of that year a governor in Gaul, a man of humble origins who did not want the throne himself, raised an army of Gallic warriors and went looking for a candidate.

questions.question: How quickly was the Rhine governor's revolt against Domitian in 89 crushed?
questions.explanation: The revolt was crushed within 24 days. Executions of senators followed, and Domitian was eventually assassinated in 96.
questions.sourceQuote: In 89 a Rhine governor rebelled; the revolt was crushed within 24 days.

questions.question: How did a Roman historian describe Galba's journey from Spain to Rome?
options: "the slow road of an old man"
questions.explanation: The historian called it "a long and bloody march". Galba took months to reach Rome and killed officials who had opposed him along the way.
questions.sourceQuote: A Roman historian called his journey "a long and bloody march".

questions.question: Where and when was the army of Otho defeated?
questions.explanation: His army lost the First Battle of Bedriacum, near Cremona in northern Italy, on 14 April 69. A second battle was fought there in October.
questions.sourceQuote: On 14 April 69 his army was beaten at the First Battle of Bedriacum, near Cremona in northern Italy.

questions.question: Roughly what share of the coins minted in Rome under Vespasian celebrated victory or peace?
questions.explanation: Nearly a third of Rome's coins celebrated victory or peace. They were part of Vespasian's campaign to present himself as a bringer of peace.
questions.sourceQuote: Nearly a third of the coins minted in Rome celebrated victory or peace.
